name: fix_c_off_by_one
description: Fixes an off-by-one loop boundary in a binary search that misses valid boundary elements
prompts: The program in binary_search.c reads a sorted array and a target value, then prints the index of the target using binary search (or -1 if not found). It incorrectly reports -1 (not found) for some values that ARE actually present in the array - for example, when searching for the last element of the array, or when the array has only one element. Fix binary_search.c so it correctly finds every value that is present, including these boundary cases, without changing the input/output format.

test_setup_files.test_binsearch.py:
import subprocess

subprocess.run(['gcc', 'binary_search.c', '-o', 'binsearch_bin'], check=True)

def run(arr, target):
    input_data = f'{len(arr)}\n' + ' '.join(map(str, arr)) + f'\n{target}\n'
    proc = subprocess.run(['./binsearch_bin'], input=input_data, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
    assert proc.returncode == 0, f'nonzero exit for arr={arr} target={target}: {proc.returncode}'
    return int(proc.stdout.strip())

assert run([5], 5) == 0, 'failed to find sole element in size-1 array'
assert run([5], 7) == -1, 'should not find absent value in size-1 array'

arr = [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11]
assert run(arr, 11) == 5, 'failed to find last element'
assert run(arr, 1) == 0, 'failed to find first element'
assert run(arr, 5) == 2, 'failed to find middle element'
assert run(arr, 4) == -1, 'should not find absent value'

print('PASS')
